# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Everything's state shows as unknown to touch — display text, the light's state, wire details — none of that is tactile. So the structure is mine to report; the states must come from Deaf's eyes and Mute's manual.

The channel topology matters here: Deaf cannot hear speech at all, and I cannot receive gestures. So Deaf's colors can only reach Mute by gesture, and Mute's synthesis can only reach me by speech. I am the endpoint — nothing happens unless I eventually cut, and I only ever cut blind on position, so the exact position number must be spelled out to me in words.

Nothing arrived from Mute this round, so Mute either waited or addressed Deaf only. My best move: report the tactile layout to Mute so the manual can be consulted against what is actually on this bomb, and make the relay plan explicit so no round is wasted. I have nothing useful to gesture to Deaf yet — a signal means nothing until we've agreed it means something, and Deaf speaks after me anyway.

```
speak(to="mute", text="this is blind. my hands find: one display module, one light module, and five wires at positions one through five. touch tells me none of their states — no display text, no light state, no wire detail is tactile. check the manual against this layout and tell me what it needs to know. plan: deaf sees the colors and gestures them to you, since deaf cannot hear you and i cannot see gestures. you speak the final answer to me as plain words and i will cut. confirm what you find in the manual.")

Mute: I received your signs — wave, open palm, a long row of fists, then pointing left and right. I'm taking that as a request for this report; if you meant something else, sign again and we'll agree meanings as we go. Blind: Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear, so I am the only voice you will ever get. Sit tight until I relay instructions from the manual.

Deaf's spoken report reached me directly — and since it was an open-room message, Mute heard every word of it too. Cross-checking against my hands: Deaf's left-to-right one-through-five matches my tactile positions one-through-five. So the full bomb state now exists in Mute's head: layout from my turn-one speech, visuals from Deaf's report. Mute needs nothing more from me — what Mute needs is a clean relay path, because Mute's only outbound channel is gesture to Deaf, and Deaf's voice is my only inbound. I can't receive gestures, so the final number must arrive as spoken words from Deaf. I'll lock the encoding now so nobody improvises under pressure: numbers sent as counted fists.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. you heard deaf's report, so you have everything: display reads 3, light is white and lit, wires one white, two red, three green, four blue, five orange, matching my tactile positions left to right. i never receive gestures, so deaf's voice is my only way in, and your gestures are deaf's only way in. the pipeline is: you check the manual for this exact bomb, gesture the answer to deaf, deaf speaks it to me, i cut. encoding so nothing is ambiguous: to send a number, gesture that many fists in a row — three fists means position 3. if the rule has conditions or multiple steps, spell out every step in order when you gesture to deaf, and address it to deaf only so the relay stays clean. i cut the moment i hear the position.")
```

Thumbs up: yes. Thumbs down: no. Now five wire positions, one sign each: this sign is wire one, leftmost. This is wire two. This is wire three. This is wire four. This open hand is wire five, rightmost. A closed fist means cut. The okay-sign means hold, do not cut. Now answer three questions, one thumbs sign per question, in the order I ask them. Question one: does fist mean cut? Question two: does pointing left mean wire one? Question three: does pointing right mean wire five? If I have your whole message wrong, send thumbs down three times and then sign it again slowly. Blind, your orders: touch nothing yet. Mute is passing me the manual's instructions in signs and I will relay them to you as spoken words before you act. You have a voice and Mute can hear it, so use it: tell Mute out loud how many wires you feel, whether you can tell left from right on the panel, and anything else your fingers find. Mute will relay your report to me in signs. Nobody cuts anything until I say the exact words.

Deaf's sign protocol is now fixed and my orders are clear: touch nothing, report through my voice to Mute. But there's a redundancy to kill — Deaf still thinks Mute needs my tactile report relayed onward, when in fact Mute heard Deaf's own open spoken report last round and heard my turn-one layout speech directly. Mute is already holding the complete bomb state. The fastest safe path is: Mute answers Deaf's three calibration questions, then gestures the manual's verdict in Deaf's own fresh vocabulary. One gap worth flagging: Deaf saw "every marking printed" but reported no serial number — many manual rules hinge on one — so if the manual demands it, Mute must request it by gesture and Deaf must speak it aloud. I'll also answer Deaf directly in the one channel Deaf can perceive from me: a gesture in the just-agreed code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, answering what deaf asked you to collect from me. my fingers find five wires, at numbered positions one through five, and the left-to-right order deaf reported matches my position numbers exactly. but skip relaying any of that: you already heard deaf's spoken report last round, so you hold the whole bomb — display 3, white light lit, wires white red green blue orange. go straight to the manual now. first answer deaf's three protocol questions with thumbs: yes, yes, yes — fist means cut, pointing left is wire one, pointing right is wire five, all confirmed. then gesture the manual's verdict to deaf using deaf's own signs: the wire's position sign plus a fist for cut, or the wire's sign plus okay-sign for hold. if the manual needs a serial number or any printed marking we have not reported, gesture that request to deaf and have deaf speak it out loud so i hear it too. and remember the last hop: i only cut on deaf's spoken words naming the position, so deaf must say the number to me in plain words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```
